start.text: {player_name}. I went to the library yesterday and borrowed last year's yearbook. Look at this.

hide.text: Or someone wanted to erase it. Hiding is keeping something somewhere else. This is different. This is making it never have existed.

start.text: Found it. At the office. I'd made a copy of the enrollment list last month, for an assignment. Compare the two.

lists.text: In the copy from a month ago, class 2-B, line 14: "Kaito Mori". In today's official list, line 14 doesn't exist. The numbering jumps from 13 to 15.
choices: I've seen that name. In my notebook.

notebook.text: In your notebook. Written by you. Before you ever saw this list. ...{player_name}, this isn't a school forgetting a student. This is the school erasing a student, and you remembering him.

initials.text: The initials on the desk. And in my notebook. He was in my class. I know he was. But I can't remember his voice. Or his face.

theory.text: From now on I'm writing everything down with the time. If the school is changing, I want to know when.
choices: Write down what I tell you too.

deal.text: Deal. Two witnesses are better than one. Even if neither of us can prove anything.

start.text: The loudspeaker called him by name. Then it said he doesn't exist. I wrote it down: 7:52. It's the first time the school has slipped backward.

theory.text: My theory: it's not the school that forgets. It's time that goes back. And every time it goes back, something doesn't come back with it. He was the first to disappear. He won't be the last.
choices: Show her the notebook in my handwriting.

impossible.text: Impossible is a word for things that haven't happened to you yet. I'll keep taking notes. You'll end up needing them.

start.text: I photographed the "DON'T GO UP" before the janitors painted over it. I compared it with the handwriting in your notebook. It's identical. And you showed up with a hurt hand, exactly as it was written.

start.text: Alice is flipping through her own notebook, faster and faster. The pages about Kaito are blank. Not erased — blank, as if they'd never been written. Only the dates are left.

blank.text: I wrote here. I know I did. I recognize where the pen pressed into the paper. But there's nothing. {player_name}, am I going crazy?
choices: No. I remember what you wrote.

truth_line.text: You know what scares me most? I used to think knowing the truth would solve things. I'm closer and closer to it, and nothing is solved. It's just heavier.

closing__2.text: "You won't beat me," she murmurs, to the watch, to the day, to no one.

start.text: I cross-referenced everything: the stopped clock, the loudspeaker, the dates in your notebook. It all points to one time. 21:47, on the night of the festival.

plan.text: Proposal: on day 12, we go up to the roof at 21:40. Seven minutes early. Just to observe. Touching nothing. Like an experiment.

agree.text: I'll sync our watches. If time goes back, at least it'll go back for both of us at once.

danger.text: Dangerous is being the only one who knows and doing nothing. But I respect it. If you change your mind, I'll have the watch ready.

poem_echo.text: Alice jots something down and remarks, without looking up: "The word '{poem_word}' shows up with a strange frequency in your writing. I liked it."

closing.text: "When someone says they don't want to know," she remarks, without looking, "I always write down the time. It's always the same time of day: right before they want to." Then she leaves, without waiting for an answer.

start.text: I finished the theory. Want to hear it? It's short. The loop starts on the first day and ends at 21:47 on day 12. What restarts it isn't time.

start__2.text: It's someone refusing to accept what happens at 21:47.

proof.text: I know the mechanism. I know the time. I know the place. And I can't do anything with it. Knowing isn't the same as being able to.
choices: But without you I wouldn't even know what I'm facing.
Maybe the answer isn't doing, but accepting.

worth.text: ...That's a nice thing to hear when you're losing. Thank you, {player_name}.

accept.text: Accepting. It's the only variable I don't know how to measure. I guess that's why I never thought of it.

start.text: Alice's notebook is almost entirely blank now. She holds it with both hands, like something that might fly away.

last.text: There's one line left. Just one. I can't read it — the letters keep moving when I look. Will you read it for me, {player_name}?

read.text: In Alice's neat handwriting, the last line says: "Trust {player_name}." Below it, a date. From a loop neither of them remembers.

trust.text: I wrote that for myself. In a loop I forgot. So... I trust you. Even without proof. That's very hard for me, you know.

closing__2.text: But this time, instead of going on, she stops and looks back: "I'm scared," she says, and it's the first time she's said it without writing it down first.

start.text: 20:58. Forty-nine minutes. I made a list of what could happen up there. Twelve scenarios. In eleven of them, I don't know what you should do.

twelfth.text: The twelfth is you doing something no other loop did. I don't know what. I only know it can't be calculated. It's the only variable that's yours.
choices: Come up with me at 21:40, like we agreed.

plan.text: As agreed. I'll stay at the door, timing it. If the clock passes 21:47, I'll shout. It'll be the happiest shout of my life.

thanks.text: I've forgotten almost everything I wrote down. But I remember it was worth writing. I think that's what matters in the end: not the answer, but having looked for it together.
